status_assessment.basis: The parish website currently advertises Holy Communion every Sunday at 9:30 am at St Bartholomew's (undated page, read 2026-09-10). Heritage NZ says it 'continues to be a place of Anglican worship'. Stuff reported the church reopening after post-earthquake restoration (about 2017), and a 2018 heritage award recognised the repair. I found no closure, sale or deconsecration evidence.
status_assessment.osm_stale_basis: The current OSM version (v3, 2026-01-31) correctly describes an active Anglican place of worship with this name and parish website. Two attributes disagree with the sources and look like original entry errors rather than staleness: start_date=1960 (sources: built 1855, moved to this site 1860) and addr:housenumber=23a (Heritage NZ: 23; Waimakariri Libraries: 23B).

Two pages returned errors: the Waimakariri Heritage (recollect) page gave HTTP 403 and the guessed Wikipedia URL gave 404. Two others gave no usable text: the Waimakariri District Council heritage PDF (HH003) came back as unparseable binary, and the Papers Past Press article of 3 April 1905 came back empty. That article was flagged by search as reporting harvest thanksgiving services at St Bartholomew's, but I could not read it, so I cite nothing from it. Only the Stuff reopening article's headline could be read; its date (about 2017) is inferred from the article id and needs checking. Two sources are outside the allowlist: DPA Architects and heritageawards.co.nz (both secondary). waimakaririlibraries.com is a council library site, but not the allowlisted waimakariri.govt.nz domain. The OSM record carries a parish office phone and email; I omitted their values under rule 5. Unresolved points for the reviewer: (1) the house number (23, 23a or 23B Cass Street); (2) OSM start_date=1960 against the 1855 build and 1860 move, probably a typo; (3) the date the church closed for earthquake repairs and the exact reopening date. Search snippets I did not open mention a first service on Christmas Day 1855 and a reopening on 20 May 1860 at Cass Street; these are not cited as evidence.
